The '''1967–68 season''' was the 69th completed season of [[The Football League|the English Football League]].

For the first time since 1937 [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] won the league title, finishing two points clear of their local rivals [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]]. [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]] finished bottom of the league and were relegated along with [[Sheffield United F.C.|Sheffield United]]. [[Coventry City F.C.|Coventry City]], in their first ever top flight season escaped relegation by one point and would go on to stay in the top division until their eventual relegation at the end of the [[2000–01 in English football|2000–01 season]].

[[Bill McGarry (footballer)|Bill McGarry]]'s [[Ipswich Town F.C.|Ipswich Town]] team won the [[Football League Second Division|Second Division]] by one point from [[Queens Park Rangers F.C.|Queens Park Rangers]], with both teams promoted. [[Blackpool F.C.|Blackpool]] finished third on goal average and so missed out. [[Rotherham United F.C.|Rotherham United]] and bottom club [[Plymouth Argyle F.C.|Plymouth Argyle]] were both relegated to the Third Division.

[[Oxford United F.C.|Oxford United]] won their first divisional title and achieved what was then their highest ever finish in only their sixth season as a league club in the [[Football League Third Division|Third Division]]. Runners-up [[Bury F.C.|Bury]] joined them in promotion. [[Grimsby Town F.C.|Grimsby Town]], [[Colchester United F.C.|Colchester United]] and [[Scunthorpe United F.C.|Scunthorpe United]] were relegated, although the biggest story concerned bottom placed [[Peterborough United F.C.|Peterborough United]] who were docked 19 points for offering irregular bonuses to their players. Had the points been restored the club would have finished in the top half. As a result of the ruling [[Mansfield Town F.C.|Mansfield Town]] escaped relegation.

[[Luton Town F.C.|Luton Town]] won the [[Football League Fourth Division|Fourth Division]] and were promoted along with [[Barnsley F.C.|Barnsley]], [[Hartlepool United F.C.|Hartlepools United]] and [[Crewe Alexandra F.C.|Crewe Alexandra]]. No clubs were voted out of the league.

==Final league tables and results==

Beginning with the season 1894–95, clubs finishing level on points were separated according to goal average (goals scored divided by goals conceded), or more properly put, goal ratio. In case one or more teams had the same goal difference, this system favoured those teams who had scored fewer goals. The goal average system was eventually replaced by goal difference, beginning with the 1976–77 season.

Since the [[Football League Fourth Division|Fourth Division]] was established in the [[1958–59 Football League|1958–59 season]], the bottom four teams of that division were required to apply for [[re-election (Football League)|re-election]].<ref name="rsssf">{{cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/engpaul/FLA/1967-68.html |title=England 1967–68 |publisher=Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation|access-date=24 February 2010}}</ref><ref name="Rothmans">Ian Laschke: ''Rothmans Book of Football League Records 1888–89 to 1978–79''. Macdonald and Jane’s, London & Sydney, 1980.</ref>
